solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: , Unofficially disliking DJ's choice?

definitions.meaning: said on the understanding that it will not be published or attributed
to be off something is to have gone off it, and the thing a disc jockey picks to play is the record

explanation.surface: Someone confides, privately, that they cannot stand the song the DJ has just put on.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: OFF means having taken against something, as in 'off your food', and THE RECORD is what the DJ chose.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes remarks given privately, not to be quoted, which is acting unofficially.

clue.text: They'll take their chance, reorganising top sport in US

indicators.note: reorganising tells us to put the letters of the following words into a new order

explanation.surface: American sporting chiefs are being reshuffled, and some people will seize the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganising' rearranges the twelve letters of TOP SPORT IN US.
explanation.definitionFit: People who exploit openings as they arise are seizing whatever chance comes along, a paraphrase.

clue.text: Dickensian villain with cigarette lit

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
a fire that is lit is said to be in, still burning

explanation.surface: A wicked Dickens character lights up a smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a fire that has not gone out is 'in', so lit gives IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The receiver of stolen goods who runs a gang of child pickpockets in Oliver Twist is a Dickens villain.

clue.text: Sixty minutes outside disreputable bar in port

indicators.note: outside means the time unit sits round the other letters

parts.note: sixty minutes make an hour

indicators.note: disreputable suggests something not in good order, so the letters of bar are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone spends an hour standing outside a seedy bar down at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disreputable' makes ARB; 'outside' is the containment signal, not a place to stand. 'in' is only a link, though it tempts you to read 'port' as something to put letters into.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltered place where ships can moor, a synonym for a port.

clue.text: Begrudge money paid to landlord round the South-East

indicators.note: round means the payment word goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a tenant's payment to a landlord is rent
SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: A tenant grumbles about paying rent in the pricey South-East of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals containment; 'the South-East' is a compass abbreviation, not the English region of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel aggrieved about something you have to give or allow is to begrudge it, a synonym.

clue.text: Constant work top journalist managed

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
op is short for opus, a musical work
ED is short for editor, the senior journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A news editor coped with relentless work.
explanation.walkthrough: OP is opus, a numbered musical work; ED is the usual crossword editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by under pressure is to have managed, a synonym in the sense of coping.

clue.text: They enjoy books about snakes on daughter rejected

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: rejected means the abbreviation for daughter is thrown out

parts.note: adders are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: Bookworms enjoy a story about snakes after a daughter is turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' removes one D, giving ADERS; in the surface it seems to be the daughter who was turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: People who enjoy books spend time reading them, which describes such people.

clue.text: Almost praise building material for a start

indicators.note: almost means the word stops just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to praise is to commend
cement is a material used in building

explanation.surface: Someone nearly praises a building material as a good place to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' leaves COMMEN; the word also means a graduation ceremony in America, but here it is just a beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginning or opening is a start, a synonym, also used for the start of an event.

clue.text: Dad has German electronic device

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: Father owns a gadget made in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeper that receives short messages is a small electronic device, an example.

clue.text: Singer in Smetana's first opera losing heart? Not so

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the composer's name
losing heart means the central letter of opera is removed

parts.note: no is a flat denial, not so

explanation.surface: A vocalist in a Smetana opera seems to lose heart, and someone disagrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives S; 'losing heart' takes the middle E out of OPERA, leaving OPRA; 'Not so' gives NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A high female singing voice, and the singer who has it, so this is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Knocked over by car? Brief report needed

definitions.meaning: a pedestrian struck by a vehicle has been ...
a quick summary of the main points

explanation.surface: After a road accident, someone needs a short account of what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into RUN DOWN, the phrase for being hit by a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A summary going quickly through the key points is a brief report, a synonym.

clue.text: Fancy Andrea making sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches says the words hold the answer between them, running across the gap

explanation.surface: Andrea is preparing some fancy sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food Andrea is making, but it is the verb: the letters sit inside anDREA Making.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to fancy something is to imagine it, a synonym of the verb meaning to imagine.

clue.text: University trained nurse lacking confidence

indicators.note: trained suggests reshaping, so the letters of nurse are reworked

explanation.surface: A university-trained nurse still doubts their abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' reads as describing the nurse's education but is the anagram signal, making NSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being doubtful of oneself or a matter means lacking confidence, a synonym.

clue.text: Superficial entertainment captivates everyone

indicators.note: captivates means the first word holds the second captive inside it

parts.note: a show is an entertainment
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A slight piece of entertainment nonetheless charms the whole audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivates' means charms in the surface but signals one word holding another.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking depth of thought or feeling is being superficial, a synonym.

clue.text: Selected socks and tights placed in empty carton

indicators.note: placed in means the hosiery word goes inside the other letters
empty leaves only the outside letters of carton

parts.note: hose is a collective word for stockings, socks and tights

explanation.surface: Chosen hosiery is packed into an empty box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' strips the carton's inner letters, and 'placed in' signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Picked out from a group means selected, a synonym.

clue.text: Hail men transforming rat-infested town

indicators.note: transforming means the letters of hail men change their arrangement

explanation.surface: People greet men changing a town overrun by rats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transforming' rearranges HAIL MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The German town of the Pied Piper legend was plagued by rats, so this is a witty description.

clue.text: Financial gain — university employee needs it

parts.note: a prof, short for professor, works at a university

explanation.surface: An academic needs money and wants to make some.
explanation.definitionFit: Money made above costs is a financial gain, a synonym.

clue.text: To sleep in centre of city is not appropriate

indicators.note: in means the sleep word sits inside the other letters
centre of takes the two middle letters of city

parts.note: to nap is to sleep briefly

explanation.surface: Taking a nap in the middle of town is not the done thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' gives IT from CITY, and NAP goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsuitable or out of place means not appropriate, a synonym.

clue.text: Ugly little creature finally bit on some bread

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of bit

parts.note: a roll is a small piece of bread

explanation.surface: An ugly little creature finally takes a bite of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives T from BIT, followed by ROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore, a misshapen goblin-like being is an ugly little creature, a description.

clue.text: Part of book on farm animal creating storm?

indicators.note: on means the book part follows the animal

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a page is part of a book

explanation.surface: A page of a farming book shows a sheep, perhaps caught in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' is a verb here: to charge about wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm about angrily or violently is to charge around wildly, a synonym.

clue.text: In the middle of Sam's songs — the middle of each

indicators.note: the middle of each takes the inner letters of both words

explanation.surface: Someone is somewhere in the midst of Sam's songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle of each' takes AM from SAM'S and ONG from SONGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being surrounded by others means being in the middle of them, a synonym.

clue.text: Castigated upper class sort pinching antique

indicators.note: pinching means the first word grips the second inside it

parts.note: toff is British slang for a posh person
antique means old

explanation.surface: A posh person is scolded for stealing an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' suggests theft, but it signals one word gripping another.
explanation.definitionFit: Being scolded or rebuked severely is to be castigated, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: After 1915 battle, English set free

indicators.note: after means the abbreviation follows the battle

parts.note: the Battle of Loos was a First World War battle in France in 1915

explanation.surface: After a First World War battle, English prisoners were released.
explanation.walkthrough: Loos is a town in northern France, scene of a British offensive in 1915.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something go or release it is to set it free, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: When to take down Christmas decorations and play

definitions.text: When to take down Christmas decorations
definitions.meaning: by tradition decorations come down on the eve of Epiphany, January 5th

explanation.surface: Someone notes when the Christmas decorations go and a play is on.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening ending the twelve days of Christmas, and also the title of a Shakespeare comedy.
